subject: Request: SLA for PilotAI preview model launch
messages:
From: Olivia Bennett <olivia@pilotai.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SLA for PilotAI preview model launch

Hi Sean,

We're planning a controlled preview of a new ranking model (internal name: pilot-rank-v2-preview) next month and would like to confirm whether Redwood can provide an uptime/latency commitment for the preview traffic. The preview will be limited to ~50k requests/day across two US regions for a 4-week window.

Specific asks:
- Can Redwood commit to a 99.0% uptime for the preview window?
- P50/P95 latency expectations for 1k token responses?
- Any carve-outs you need for beta model behavior?

We're ok with an explicit SLA exception if needed, but need documented guardrails so we can align with our internal compliance. Also: can you share any telemetry from your internal run of the model (latency and error-rate samples)?

Thanks — Olivia
Olivia Bennett
Head of Platform
PilotAI

--
Follow-up: we might need a DocuSign on any temporary exception.
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Bennett <olivia@pilotai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jan 2026 11:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA for PilotAI preview model launch

Hi Olivia — thanks for the detail. Short answer: we can support the preview but we typically do not extend our standard 99.9% hosted SLA to models in preview/beta. What we can offer for a preview:

- A documented SLA exception that sets uptime at 99.0% for the preview window with these guardrails:
  - Timeboxed: explicit start/end dates and telemetry review 
  - Scoped: only for pilot-rank-v2-preview on your account and two US regions
  - Operational controls: reduced concurrency cap (to reduce risk of tail latency events) and automatic fallback to our stable rank model if error rate > X%
- Expected latencies (from our internal perf runs): p50 ~ 120ms, p95 ~ 420ms for 1k-token ranked responses on c5d-like instances with batching enabled — we'll attach the telemetry CSV. Real-world latency will vary; we recommend a 50-100ms buffer for integration.
- Exceptions: we reserve the right to route traffic off preview model for sustained degradation; we'll provide timely notification and a post-mortem if that happens.

I'll loop in Lauren and Markus to approve a timeboxed SLA exception and sign-off on the fallbacks. I attached a short SLA Proposal draft and the telemetry you asked for.

Next steps: if that looks acceptable I can send a formal DocuSign with the exception terms and a mutual action plan.

Best,
Sean Gallagher

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: pilot-rank-v2-preview — request for SLA exception (PilotAI)

Team — PilotAI is asking for a 99.0% uptime commit for a 4-week preview. Traffic: ~50k req/day, two US regions. Their engineering lead may require a signed DocuSign exception to satisfy compliance.

Operational notes and risk controls I'm proposing:
- Timebox the exception: 2026-02-09 to 2026-03-08
- Concurrency cap: 40 concurrent requests/account for the preview
- Autoscaling policy: restrict burst above baseline to operator-approved bursts only
- Fallback: automatic routing to stable 'rank-v1' if error rate > 1.5% sustained for 5 minutes
- Telemetry: PilotAI will get a daily CSV and we'll run a mid-preview performance check at 2 weeks

Impact: increases support-sla touchpoints; ops will pre-warm slots for their expected traffic. We should also offer a credit mechanism tied to prolonged outages (outside carve-outs).

Can I get an approval or suggested changes? I want to respond to Olivia by EOD Monday with a signed DocuSign plan if approved.

Thanks — Sean
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 08:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: pilot-rank-v2-preview — request for SLA exception (PilotAI)

Sean — fine to proceed with the exception using your proposed guardrails with two modifications:
1) Add explicit notification windows: 30-minute heads-up for traffic routing changes and a 4-hour window for non-emergency operator-initiated capacity adjustments.
2) Define credits: if uptime for preview falls below 99.0% for the period (excluding carve-outs) issue a 10% service credit on the monthly bill for the preview period.

Markus/Dev — please confirm we can implement the fallback threshold (1.5% error sustained for 5 minutes) and the concurrency cap with no service-side regressions. If ops needs an alternative threshold, propose it by EOD.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Bennett <olivia@pilotai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 15 Jan 2026 16:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA for PilotAI preview model launch — exception terms and next steps

Olivia — thanks for waiting. We've approved a timeboxed SLA exception for the pilot-rank-v2-preview with the following summary: 

Summary of agreed terms (preview exception):
- Window: 2026-02-09T00:00:00Z through 2026-03-08T23:59:59Z
- Uptime commitment: 99.0% for the preview window (carve-outs listed below)
- Latency guidance: p50 ~120ms, p95 ~420ms for 1k-token ranked responses; recommend a 50–100ms buffer in your client
- Operational controls: concurrency cap 40 per account; autoscale bursts require operator sign-off; automatic fallback to stable rank-v1 if error rate >1.5% sustained for 5 minutes
- Notification windows: 30-minute notice for emergency routing; 4-hour window for non-emergency capacity changes
- Credits: 10% service credit on the invoice for the preview period if uptime < 99.0% (excluding agreed carve-outs)

Carve-outs: scheduled maintenance, force majeure, customer traffic patterns causing cascading failures, and known model instability due to their experimental input distributions.

Attachments: I attached the SLA-Proposal-PilotAI-preview-v1.1.pdf and the telemetry CSV. Next step: if you accept these terms we'll send a short DocuSign template with the exception and the mutual action plan (dates, contact points, runbook). Please confirm and I will route the DocuSign.

Best regards,
Sean
